sentence: Mara glaubt, dass der erfahrene Lehrer den schwierigen Bericht sorgfältig lesen wird.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The analysis uses NP, VP, IP, and CP projections in Government and Binding Theory. German VP and IP are head-final; CP has a head preceding its IP complement. In both clauses, the subject originates in Spec-VP. Glaubt selects the propositional CP introduced by dass, and the future auxiliary wird selects the infinitival VP headed by lesen. The manner adverb sorgfältig is left-adjoined to the lexical V-bar: it characterizes reading, not believing or the future auxiliary. At this base stage it precedes the object; the object's eventual position before the adverb will be derived by local scrambling. Determiners occupy nominal specifiers, while attributive APs adjoin to N-bar. The inflected words are represented as whole lexical terminals, so no separate morphological realization groups are required. Their lexical inflection does not imply that the syntactic Case and agreement dependencies have already been established. Lesen assigns the report NP its internal theta role and accusative Case in its complement position. The teacher and Mara receive external theta roles in their respective VP specifiers. Finite I heads are initially silent feature-bearing heads, and the matrix clause has not yet acquired its V2 CP structure.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the head-final base structure and the lexical argument relations.

values.movement: future auxiliary to head-final finite I

derivationStages.stageRecord: The teacher NP raises from the lexical VP specifier to Spec-IP, leaving an NP trace in its theta position. Finite I licenses nominative Case and agrees with this third-person singular subject. The auxiliary then moves from its VP-final head position to the adjacent, head-final I position, leaving a head trace. This analysis adopts V-to-I movement in the German subordinate clause; it does not move the auxiliary to C because dass already heads the embedded CP. The resulting complex I contains the pronounced whole word wird and the silent finite features. Both movement origins were present in the preceding workspace. The object remains in its original complement position, so its surface order relative to the manner adverb is not yet derived.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the embedded subject's nominative position and the clause-final finite auxiliary.

relations.relation: local object scrambling and trace binding

values.movement: V-complement to left-adjoined lexical VP position

derivationStages.stageRecord: The accusative report NP moves from the complement of lesen to a left-adjoined position on the lexical VP. Its source is replaced by an NP trace, still governed by lesen and connected to the moved NP by the scrambling chain. This is a local, clause-internal adjunction analysis of German scrambling, not movement into the embedded CP. It preserves the object's original theta role and accusative Case. Because the teacher has already raised to Spec-IP, the resulting order is der erfahrene Lehrer, den schwierigen Bericht, sorgfältig, lesen, wird. The adverb remains attached to the reading predicate; its interpretation has not been reassigned merely to obtain this order.
derivationStages.statement: Derive the embedded object-before-adverb order by local scrambling.

values.movement: lexical verb to head-final finite I

derivationStages.stageRecord: Mara raises from the matrix VP specifier to Spec-IP, leaving a theta-position trace. Matrix finite I assigns nominative Case and agrees with the third-person singular subject. Glaubt then moves from the head-final matrix V position into I, leaving a V trace. The whole inflected word is carried by the moved verbal head; the silent I feature head adds no separate pronounced material. The embedded CP remains the selected complement of the matrix verb and retains its completed subordinate-clause structure. This intermediate IP must be recorded because the next head movement starts from I rather than directly from the lexical V position.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the matrix subject's Case position and move the finite lexical verb to I.

values.movement: finite I to declarative matrix C

derivationStages.stageRecord: A declarative matrix CP is projected over the existing IP. Its initially silent C head hosts the complex finite I head, which moves from the position explicitly established in the previous stage and leaves an I trace. This successive V-to-I-to-C derivation respects the intervening head position. The pronounced verb is now in the matrix left bracket, while the embedded complement remains in the matrix VP. Spec-CP is not yet filled, so this stage establishes verb placement but not the completed subject-initial V2 order. Unlike the matrix clause, the dass clause retains its overt complementizer and clause-final finite I.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the matrix CP and move the finite I head to C.

relations.relation: matrix prefield A-bar movement and trace binding

values.surfaceConfiguration: one prefield constituent followed by the finite verb in C

derivationStages.stageRecord: Mara moves from the already established Spec-IP position to Spec-CP, leaving a second NP trace. This A-bar movement fills the matrix prefield; it need not imply contrastive emphasis. Its nominative Case and theta interpretation remain inherited through the earlier A-chain. The completed matrix order is Mara followed by glaubt in C and the selected dass clause. Within that clause, the nominative subject precedes the locally scrambled accusative object, the manner adverb modifies lesen, and wird occupies final I. The trace chains preserve each argument's theta position and each moved head's source. All supplied words are pronounced exactly once in their indexed order. The comma and period belong to the written sentence but are not separate supplied tokens or syntactic terminals.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the subject-initial matrix V2 clause and the full input analysis.
